mainTopic: No כיסוי הדם for consecrated birds or for a בהמה, and the תורה's lessons of דרך ארץ about eating meat and spending wisely
overview: The amud opens by explaining why there is no כיסוי הדם for a bird consecrated for בדק הבית. It cannot be redeemed after slaughter, because redemption needs העמדה והערכה. רב יוסף shows that this follows רבי, who takes one point from רבי מאיר and one from רבי שמעון. A second answer uses the פסוק ״וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה״: covering applies only when nothing comes between pouring and covering. The same answer works for קדשי מזבח too. מר בר רב אשי learns the same exemption from ״חַיָּה אוֹ עוֹף״. רבא then answers יעקב מינאה that a בהמה's blood is poured 'like water' and needs no covering, and the גמרא proves from the מקוה פסוק that blood still cannot purify. Next, ברייתות learn lessons of דרך ארץ about meat: eat it with effort and real appetite, from your own animals, and never use up everything you own. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gives a food-spending scale, and רב, רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן discuss it. The amud closes with money lessons from a פסוק in משלי and opens a statement by רבי יוחנן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not redeem the birds and then cover the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if these are birds of בדק הבית, just redeem them after slaughter, and then cover their blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him redeem them, and then cover their blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that there is no כיסוי הדם for these consecrated birds. It suggests that after slaughter, the bird could be redeemed and become regular, so its blood should be covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds of בדק הבית are not meant for the מזבח, so they can normally be redeemed. If redeeming them after slaughter made the meat permitted, then the slaughter would count as a fitting slaughter. That would bring back the duty of כיסוי הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him redeem them (פִּדְיוֹן): trade the holy status onto money so the animal becomes regular.
Let him cover them, meaning cover their blood (כִּסּוּי הַדָּם).
Upkeep of the בית המקדש. Things given for this are valued for their money, not brought on the מזבח.

phrases.english: But let him redeem them and cover them!
phrases.notes: "Cover them" means cover their blood, the מצוה of כיסוי הדם.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפְרְקִינְהוּ וְלִיכַסִּינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by challenging the earlier claim that birds of בדק הבית need no כיסוי הדם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that slaughtering birds of בדק הבית does not require כיסוי הדם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds of בדק הבית can be redeemed. Redeeming them after slaughter would make them permitted, so the blood should be covered.

steps.title: Redemption needs standing and valuing
steps.stepSummary: Redemption is not possible after slaughter, because it requires standing the animal before a כהן and valuing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need standing and valuing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: a dead bird cannot be redeemed, because redemption requires העמדה והערכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem a consecrated animal, it must be stood before a כהן so he can set its value. A slaughtered bird cannot stand, so it cannot be redeemed. That means it can never become permitted, and there is no כיסוי הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: We need / we require.
Standing the animal before a כהן and valuing it. This is required before redemption (ויקרא 27:11–12).

phrases.english: We require setting and valuating.
phrases.notes: The animal must be alive and stood before a כהן to be valued (ויקרא 27:11–12), and a slaughtered bird can't be.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵינַן הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a legal barrier: redemption has a requirement that cannot be met.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the slaughtered bird could simply be redeemed and then made permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Redemption needs העמדה והערכה, which is impossible after slaughter. So the bird cannot be redeemed, and there is no כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: It cannot follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this is. רבי מאיר agrees about העמדה והערכה, but he holds that even an unfitting slaughter counts as slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose view is this? If it is רבי מאיר, who says everything was included in standing and valuing, doesn't he also say that a slaughter which is not fitting is still called a slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks which תנא this ruling follows. It tests רבי מאיר first and shows he can't be the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that all consecrated animals, even בדק הבית ones, need העמדה והערכה, which fits step 2. But he also holds that a slaughter which does not permit the meat still counts as slaughter. By that view, the blood would need covering anyway, even without redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: And like whom? Whose view does this follow?
Included in (a rule or requirement).
A slaughter that is not fitting, meaning it does not make the meat permitted to eat.
It is called a slaughter, so it still counts legally, for example for כיסוי הדם.
But doesn't he say...? Used to point out a problem from the same sage's other view.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two separate questions. Question A: does a בדק הבית animal need העמדה והערכה? Question B: does an unfitting slaughter count as slaughter? The ruling here needs 'yes' to A and 'no' to B.

phrases.english: And in accordance with whom?
If like Rabbi Meir, who says:
Everything was included in setting and valuating,
phrases.notes: "Everything" means animals for the מזבח and animals for בדק הבית alike.

phrases.english: doesn't he say: a slaughter that is not fit
is called a slaughter!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְמַאן? אִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 2 and asks which תנא it fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying the ruling follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר holds that an unfitting slaughter still counts as slaughter, so he would require כיסוי הדם even without redemption.

steps.title: It cannot follow רבי שמעון either
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון agrees that an unfitting slaughter is not a slaughter, but he holds that בדק הבית animals do not need העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי שמעון, who says a slaughter that is not fitting is not called a slaughter, doesn't he also say that they were not included in standing and valuing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the other option, רבי שמעון, and shows he can't be the source either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees with the first half: an unfitting slaughter does not count, so כיסוי הדם depends on whether the bird could become permitted. But he holds that בדק הבית animals do not need העמדה והערכה. So the dead bird could be redeemed, and the blood should be covered. Now neither תנא fits the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not called a slaughter; it does not count legally.

phrases.english: If like Rabbi Shimon, who says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה –
phrases.english: a slaughter that is not fit is not called a slaughter,
doesn't he say: they were not
included in setting and valuating?
phrases.notes: "They" means animals given to בדק הבית, so by his view a slaughtered bird could still be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the two-sided question that step 3 began.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying the ruling follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון holds that בדק הבית animals do not need העמדה והערכה, so the slaughtered bird could be redeemed and its blood covered.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is רבי, taking one view from each
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the ruling is רבי's. He follows רבי שמעון on unfitting slaughter and רבי מאיר on העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is רבי, and he formulated it according to different תנאים. On a slaughter that is not fitting, he holds like רבי שמעון. On standing and valuing, he holds like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the problem. The ruling belongs to רבי, who mixes the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי שמעון, an unfitting slaughter does not count, so כיסוי הדם is needed only if the bird can become permitted. Like רבי מאיר, even בדק הבית animals need העמדה והערכה, so a slaughtered bird can never be redeemed. Put together, there is never a duty of כיסוי הדם here.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes it according to different תנאים, combining the views of different sages.
He holds (a certain view).

steps.whatToRemember: No כיסוי הדם for a slaughtered בדק הבית bird, because of רבי's mix. From רבי שמעון: an unfitting slaughter is not a slaughter. From רבי מאיר: all consecrated animals need העמדה והערכה. So the bird can never become permitted, and its slaughter never counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא move: when no single תנא fits a ruling, רבי, who arranged the משנה, may have taken each separate point from a different sage.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is Rabbi,
phrases.notes: "רבי" here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: and he takes it according to different tanna'im;
regarding a slaughter that is not fit,
he holds like Rabbi Shimon;
regarding setting and valuating,
he holds like Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי הִיא, וְנָסֵיב לַהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided problem of steps 3–4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ruling to a third תנא who combines parts of two opposing views.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling had to follow either רבי מאיר or רבי שמעון, and each one fails on one point.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי follows רבי שמעון on unfitting slaughter and רבי מאיר on העמדה והערכה. So the bird can't be redeemed, the slaughter doesn't count, and there is no כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: The whole ruling can follow רבי שמעון, learned from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Even if we follow רבי שמעון, these birds are exempt from covering. The פסוק requires covering only when nothing comes between pouring and covering, and here פדייה comes in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say the whole ruling is רבי שמעון. Here it is different, because the פסוק says 'and he shall pour out and cover.' That means only blood that needs nothing except pouring and covering. This one is left out, because it needs pouring, then redemption, then covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to answer the question from Step 1, without needing רבי's mixed view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says בדק הבית birds can be redeemed even after slaughter, so the question 'why not redeem and then cover?' comes back. The answer is a new rule from the פסוק: covering applies only when covering comes right after pouring the blood. Here a step of פדייה would have to come in between, so there is no obligation to cover.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
Pouring out the blood during slaughter
Covering the blood (כיסוי הדם)
Lacking; still needing another step
Redemption of הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גמרא does not say the redemption fails. Under רבי שמעון it works. The exemption comes only because redemption would come between pouring and covering.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
the whole of it is Rabbi Shimon's,
and here it is different,
for the verse says: "And he shall pour out and cover",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:13

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּסָּר אֶלָּא שְׁפִיכָה וְכִסּוּי,
phrases.english: one that is lacking only pouring and covering,
this one is excluded,
which is lacking pouring, redemption, and covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of רב יוסף's answer that the ruling is רבי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of a פסוק that makes the exemption independent of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If בדק הבית birds can be redeemed after slaughter, as רבי שמעון holds, one should redeem them and then cover the blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Covering applies only when nothing comes between pouring and covering. Redemption would come in between, so these birds are exempt.

steps.title: The same rule explains birds of קדשי מזבח
steps.stepSummary: With this new rule, the ruling can even be about birds consecrated for the מזבח. Scraping their blood off the מזבח would come between pouring and covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say it is talking about קדשי מזבח. Only blood that needs nothing except pouring and covering must be covered. This one is left out, because it needs pouring, then scraping, then covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the new rule from Step 6 and uses it to answer the earlier question about קדשי מזבח as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא asked why one could not scrape the blood of a bird קרבן off the מזבח and then cover it. The same rule answers this: scraping is an extra step between pouring and covering, so there is no obligation. One rule now covers both kinds of הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that you have come to this: an earlier answer is now extended further
Animals consecrated to be brought on the מזבח
Scraping the blood off the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Under this approach, the פסוק ״וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה״ requires covering only when it follows the pouring directly. Any step in between, like פדייה or גרירה, means there is no obligation.

phrases.english: And now that you have come to this,
you can even say it is about animals consecrated for the altar,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּסָּר אֶלָּא שְׁפִיכָה וְכִסּוּי –
phrases.english: one that is lacking only pouring and covering
this one is excluded,
which is lacking pouring, scraping, and covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from Step 6 to קדשי מזבח as well.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending a rule to a second case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For קדשי מזבח, one could scrape the blood off the מזבח and then cover it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Scraping is an extra step between pouring and covering, so there is no obligation to cover.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי learns the exemption from ״חַיָּה אוֹ עוֹף״
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי gives another source. The פסוק puts חיה next to עוף. Just as a חיה is never קודש, the bird in the פסוק is also one that is not קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: The פסוק says 'a חיה or a bird.' Just as a חיה is not holy, so too the bird is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא brings a different source for why הקדש birds are exempt from covering their blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of focusing on the order of pouring and covering, מר בר רב אשי compares the two creatures named together in the פסוק. A חיה can never be a קרבן. So the bird the פסוק is talking about must also be a non-holy bird, and holy birds are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild animal, such as a deer, which can never be a קרבן
Bird
Holy; consecrated
Just as ... so too: a comparison between two cases

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
the verse says: "a wild animal or a bird",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:13

phrases.english: just as a wild animal is not holy,
so too the bird is not holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אָמַר קְרָא ״חַיָּה אוֹ עוֹף״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a completely different source than ״וְשָׁפַךְ וְכִסָּה״ for the same exemption.
steps.raayaObject: That birds which are הקדש are exempt from כיסוי הדם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק ״חַיָּה אוֹ עוֹף״ in ויקרא 17:13, comparing bird to חיה

steps.title: Challenge: the comparison would exclude all doves and pigeons
steps.stepSummary: If we compare bird to חיה, we could say: a חיה is a species that can never be holy. Then only birds of a species that can never be holy would count, and even ordinary doves and pigeons would be left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe: just as a חיה is a species that can never be holy, so too the bird must be a species that can never be holy. Then I would leave out turtledoves and young pigeons, whose species can be holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks מר בר רב אשי's comparison by showing it could be stretched too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison could be about the individual bird, meaning this bird is not holy. Or it could be about the whole species, meaning this kind of bird can never be holy. If it means the species, then even non-holy תורין ובני יונה would not need their blood covered, which cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: In its species; its kind
Turtledoves, a kind of bird that can be a קרבן
Young pigeons, also a kind of bird that can be a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not about holy doves. It is about ordinary, non-holy doves and pigeons, which would wrongly lose the מצוה just because their species can be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: If so, just as a wild animal
is one whose species has nothing holy,
so too a bird whose species has nothing holy,
so I will exclude turtledoves and young pigeons,
whose species does include holy ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה חַיָּה שֶׁאֵין בְּמִינוֹ קֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison in Step 8 should be taken.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's comparison of עוף to חיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is about the species and not the individual bird, it would wrongly exempt ordinary תורין ובני יונה from כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: The comparison to a חיה means no species of bird is left out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects Step 9's reading. Comparing bird to חיה teaches that, just as every kind of חיה is included, every kind of bird is included too.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Compare the bird to a חיה this way: just as with a חיה you made no split between its kinds, so too with a bird you should make no split between its kinds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 9. It explains what the comparison between bird and חיה really teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 worried that the comparison would leave out any bird species that can ever be holy, such as doves and pigeons. The גמרא says the point of the comparison is different. A חיה gets covering with no split between its kinds, so every kind of bird gets covering too. Only a bird that is actually holy is left out, as מר בר רב אשי taught in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: You did not split or make a distinction (between kinds)
You shall not split or make a distinction

steps.whatToRemember: The bird is compared to a חיה to teach that no kind of bird is excluded. Doves and pigeons that are not holy still need כיסוי הדם.

phrases.english: No, it is like a wild animal:
just as with a wild animal you did not make a split between its kinds,
so too with a bird, you shall not make a split between its kinds.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, כְּחַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by giving a different meaning to the comparison of bird to חיה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the comparison: it is about not splitting species, not about a species that can never be holy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison would leave out any species of bird that can ever be holy, including doves and pigeons
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison teaches that no kind of bird is left out, just as no kind of חיה is left out

steps.title: יעקב the heretic asks why a בהמה does not count as a חיה for covering
steps.stepSummary: יעקב מינאה tells רבא: a חיה is included as a בהמה for the kosher signs, so let a בהמה also be included as a חיה for כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: יעקב the heretic said to רבא: We hold that a חיה is included in the group 'בהמה' for the kosher signs. So I will also say that a בהמה is included in the group 'חיה' for covering the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. יעקב מינאה asks why the blood of a בהמה, such as a cow or sheep, should not need covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists the kosher signs under בהמה, and we know those signs also apply to a חיה. יעקב argues that if the two groups can cover each other in one area, they should work both ways. Then a בהמה would also need כיסוי, just like a חיה.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, someone who rejects the rabbis' teachings
We hold, it is established for us
Included in the group of
The kosher signs (chewing the cud and split hooves)
Covering the blood after slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: A בהמה is a domestic animal like a cow or sheep. A חיה is a wild animal like a deer. Only a חיה and a bird need their blood covered.

phrases.english: Yaakov the heretic said to Rava:
We hold
that a wild animal is included in 'domestic animal' for the kosher signs.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא נָמֵי בְּהֵמָה בִּכְלַל חַיָּה לְכִסּוּי.
phrases.english: I will also say that a domestic animal is included in 'wild animal' for covering the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ יַעֲקֹב מִינָאָה לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whether כיסוי הדם applies to a בהמה
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a בהמה does not need כיסוי הדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the groups overlap in one direction (a חיה counts as a בהמה for the kosher signs), they should overlap in the other direction too (a בהמה counts as a חיה for covering)

steps.title: רבא: a בהמה's blood is poured out like water, so it needs no covering
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the פסוק about a בהמה, 'pour it on the ground like water.' Water needs no covering, so this blood needs no covering either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Against your claim the פסוק says, 'On the ground you shall pour it, like water.' Just as water does not need covering, so this blood also does not need covering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers יעקב with a פסוק that is said about the blood of a בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the blood of a slaughtered בהמה to water poured on the ground. Nobody covers spilled water, so the תורה is telling us this blood is also left uncovered. A פסוק like this overrides the logical argument that the groups should overlap both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Against your claim the פסוק says
You shall pour it out
Like water
Requires, needs

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that a בהמה, such as a cow or sheep, needs no כיסוי הדם.

phrases.english: He said to him: Against your claim, the verse says:
"On the ground you shall pour it, like water".
phrases.notes: דברים 12:24. The פסוק there is talking about slaughtering cattle and sheep.

phrases.english: Just as water does not need covering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַאי נָמֵי לָא בָּעֵי כִּסּוּי.
phrases.english: so too this one also does not need covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָלֶיךָ אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers יעקב מינאה's challenge with a פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the logical comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בהמה should count as a חיה and need כיסוי
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood of a בהמה is like water and needs no covering

steps.title: If blood is like water, should it work for טבילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's comparison: if this blood is like water, maybe impure things could be immersed in it to make them pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, let people immerse things in it for purity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes רבא's comparison to see if it goes too far. If blood is like water for covering, is it also like water for טבילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water can purify impure things through טבילה. If the פסוק makes a בהמה's blood equal to water, maybe it equals water in every way, including for purifying. That would be a strange result, so the גמרא asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, according to your logic
Let them immerse (impure items to purify them)

phrases.english: But if so, let them immerse items in it?
phrases.notes: 'In it' means in the blood, since the פסוק just compared it to water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, יַטְבִּילוּ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far רבא's comparison to water goes
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's comparison of a בהמה's blood to water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the blood is like water, it should be like water in every way, including purifying through טבילה

steps.title: Only real bodies of water purify, not blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק 'Only a spring or a pit, a gathering of water, shall be pure.' Only these purify, and nothing else does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'Only a spring or a pit, a gathering of water, shall be pure.' These purify; nothing else does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A separate פסוק limits טבילה to real water sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אך ('only') in the פסוק about purifying shuts out everything except a spring, a pit, or a gathered body of water. So the comparison of blood to water works for covering, but it cannot make blood purify. The comparison stands, and the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Only, a word that limits
A natural spring
A pit or cistern
A gathering of water, a מקוה
These, yes (they work)

steps.whatToRemember: A בהמה's blood is like water, so it needs no covering. But only real water purifies, so blood cannot be used for טבילה.

phrases.english: The verse says: "Only a spring or a pit,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:36. The word אך ('only') is what limits it.

phrases.english: a gathering of water, shall be pure".
These, yes; anything else, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״אַךְ מַעְיָן וּבוֹר מִקְוֵה מַיִם יִהְיֶה טָהוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 with a limiting פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word (אך) in a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood is like water for everything, so it should purify through טבילה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a spring, a pit, or a gathering of water purifies, so blood does not

steps.title: Maybe the exclusion only removes other liquids, not blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 14: the word 'only' might exclude other liquids that are never called water, but blood is called water and might still purify.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that this exclusion only removes other liquids, which are not called water. Blood, which is called water, may indeed purify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 14. It argues that the exclusion in the פסוק may not cover blood at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said only a spring, pit or gathering of water purifies. The challenge is that 'only' could mean 'only water, not other liquids.' Since the תורה called בהמה blood 'like water,' maybe blood counts as water for a מקוה too.

keyTerms.meaning: This matter / this rule applies (only to a certain case)
To exclude
Other liquids (wine, oil, milk, etc.)
So too / indeed it would be so

phrases.english: But say: this matter
phrases.notes: He means the word 'only' in the מקוה פסוק from Step 14.

phrases.english: is to exclude other liquids,
which are not called water,
but blood, which is called water,
phrases.notes: Going back to רבא's פסוק: 'pour it on the ground like water.'

phrases.english: so too [it would purify]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁאָר מַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the exclusion given in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 14 that the word 'only' rules out blood as a purifying liquid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion may be limited to liquids not called water. Blood is called water, so it may fall outside the exclusion.

steps.title: There are two exclusions in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק has two limiting phrases, 'a spring of water' and 'a pit of water,' so the extra one can exclude blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two exclusions are written: 'a spring of water' and 'a pit of water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out that the פסוק limits things twice, not once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One limiting phrase is used up on excluding other liquids. The second limiting phrase is extra, so it is used to exclude blood as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Two exclusions / two limiting phrases
A spring
A pit or cistern

phrases.english: Two exclusions are written:
'A spring of water' and 'a pit of water.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:36. The word 'water' is read as going with each item, so each one counts as its own limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי מִיעוּטֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra exclusion in the פסוק (an extra מיעוט)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one exclusion exists, and it covers only other liquids.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two exclusions exist. One excludes other liquids and the other excludes blood.

steps.title: Both exclusions may be needed for other liquids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: both exclusions might be about other liquids. One excludes flowing liquids, and the other excludes gathered liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that both of them exclude other liquids: one excludes flowing liquids and one excludes gathered liquids!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 16 by finding a different job for the second exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spring purifies even while flowing, and a pit purifies when its water is gathered. So the גמרא suggests that 'spring' excludes other flowing liquids and 'pit' excludes other gathered liquids. That leaves nothing extra to exclude blood.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one / both of them
Flowing liquids
Gathered (standing) liquids

phrases.english: Say: both this one and that one
are to exclude other liquids,
one to exclude flowing ones,
phrases.notes: This goes with 'spring,' which purifies even while it flows.

phrases.english: and one to exclude gathered ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁאָר מַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the second exclusion is extra and so excludes blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both exclusions are needed for other liquids, one for flowing and one for gathered. No exclusion is left over for blood.

steps.title: There are three exclusions, and the third excludes blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק actually has three limiting phrases: spring, pit and gathering of water. The third one excludes blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three exclusions are written: 'a spring of water,' 'a pit of water,' and 'a gathering of water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question by counting a third limiting phrase in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Spring' excludes other flowing liquids, and 'pit' excludes other gathered liquids. 'Gathering of water' is a third exclusion, so it excludes blood. This shows that even though blood is called 'like water' for כיסוי הדם, it cannot purify in a מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Three exclusions / three limiting phrases
A gathering of water (a מקוה)

steps.whatToRemember: Blood is compared to water only for not needing covering. The three limits in 'מעין, בור, מקוה מים' show it cannot purify like a מקוה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the comparison to water makes blood count as water for everything. The comparison teaches one thing only: this blood does not need to be covered.

phrases.english: Three exclusions are written:
'A spring of water,' 'a pit of water,' 'a gathering of water.'
phrases.notes: The first two cover other flowing and gathered liquids, and the third one excludes blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּלָתָא מִיעוּטֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17 and closes the discussion begun in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A third exclusion in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only two exclusions exist, and both are used up on other liquids.
steps.terutzMaskana: A third exclusion, 'a gathering of water,' excludes blood from purifying.

steps.title: Does covering the blood apply to animals that are already 'trapped'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the פסוק says 'who traps.' It asks how we know that birds which never need trapping, like geese and chickens, also need כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: the פסוק says 'who traps.' That only covers animals a person actually traps. How do we know the rule also applies to animals that are already 'trapped' on their own, like geese and chickens?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא about the מצוה of כיסוי הדם. It asks a question: the פסוק says 'who traps,' so does the מצוה also apply to birds that are never hunted?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'who traps' sounds like the מצוה applies only to a חיה or עוף that a person actually hunts. Geese and chickens live in the yard and never need to be caught. So the ברייתא asks where we learn that they are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only have…': the plain words of the פסוק only teach this much
Already standing trapped, meaning birds that never need to be caught
Geese and chickens
From where do we know?

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "Who traps"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:13, the פסוק about covering the blood of a חיה or עוף.

phrases.english: I only have [the case of] what one traps.
Those that are already trapped on their own: from where [do we know]?
Such as geese and chickens?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֲשֶׁר יָצוּד, נִצּוֹדִין וְעוֹמְדִין מֵאֲלֵיהֶן מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא on a new topic, after the discussion of what purifies ended in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that כיסוי הדם applies even to birds that need no trapping.

steps.title: The word 'a trapping' includes every case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the word ציד teaches that the מצוה applies in every case, whether or not the animal was hunted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'a trapping,' meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The extra word ציד shows that כיסוי הדם applies to every kosher חיה and עוף, even ones that were never hunted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says both 'who traps' and 'a trapping.' The ברייתא reads the word ציד as widening the rule, so geese and chickens are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches by saying…': it introduces the source
'A trapping,' a hunted animal
In any case, no matter what

phrases.english: The verse says "a trapping":
in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״צֵיד״, מִכׇּל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ציד includes all cases, so even geese and chickens need כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say 'who traps'?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule applies in every case, the words 'who traps' seem to teach nothing. So why does the פסוק include them?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the פסוק teach by saying 'who traps'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks about its own answer. If ציד already includes everything, the words 'who traps' look unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא works on the idea that every word in the תורה has a purpose. Since 'who traps' does not limit the הלכה, it must be teaching something else. This question prepares the way for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if what you just said is true
Why does the פסוק need to say this?

phrases.english: If so,
what does the verse teach by saying "who traps"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר יָצוּד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 20. Since ציד includes everything, the words 'who traps' now need a purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the words אשר יצוד, since they do not limit the הלכה.

steps.title: Meat should come with effort, like something hunted
steps.stepSummary: The words 'who traps' teach דרך ארץ: a person should eat meat only with this kind of preparation, as if it had to be hunted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה taught proper conduct: a person should eat meat only with this kind of preparation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'who traps' is not a הלכה about כיסוי הדם. It is a lesson in good behavior about how often to eat meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hunted animal is not always at hand; it takes real effort to get. The תורה hints that meat should be treated the same way: not something a person eats all the time, but something that takes preparation.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה taught proper, sensible behavior
Preparation, getting something ready
Meat

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rule about which animals need כיסוי הדם. That was already settled in Step 20. It is advice about good habits.

phrases.english: The Torah taught proper conduct:
that a person should not eat meat
except with this kind of preparation.
phrases.notes: 'This preparation' means the effort of hunting. Meat shouldn't be something you just grab all the time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִמְּדָה תּוֹרָה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאכַל אָדָם בָּשָׂר אֶלָּא בַּהַזְמָנָה הַזֹּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words אשר יצוד teach the דרך ארץ of eating meat only with effort and preparation.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a word in the תורה which does not change the הלכה can still teach a lesson about how to live.

steps.title: Eat meat only when you really want it
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from 'When ה׳ expands your border' that a person should eat meat only out of real appetite.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: 'When ה׳ your God expands your border.' The תורה taught proper conduct: a person should eat meat only when he has an appetite for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with a similar lesson of דרך ארץ about meat, this time from a פסוק in דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק allows eating meat when a person's soul craves it. The ברייתא reads this as guidance: eat meat when you truly want it, not out of habit.

keyTerms.meaning: When [ה׳] expands
Your border, your territory
Out of appetite, because one really wants it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"When ה׳ your God expands your border"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:20. The פסוק goes on to say you may eat meat when you crave it.

phrases.english: The Torah taught proper conduct:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאכַל אָדָם בָּשָׂר אֶלָּא לְתֵאָבוֹן.
phrases.english: that a person should not eat meat except out of appetite.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״כִּי יַרְחִיב ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת גְּבֻלְךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא with another lesson of דרך ארץ about eating meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should eat meat only when he truly has an appetite for it.

steps.title: May one just buy meat from the market?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that a person might simply buy meat in the market and eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person may take meat from the market and eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible idea, a 'you might have thought,' so that the next פסוק can answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only rule were to eat meat out of appetite, a person could easily buy it whenever he liked. The ברייתא tests whether that is the proper way.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought: a possible idea that will be checked
Marketplace

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יִקַּח אָדָם מִן הַשּׁוּק וְיֹאכַל?
phrases.english: You might think a person may take [meat] from the market and eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִקַּח אָדָם מִן הַשּׁוּק וְיֹאכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a 'you might think' idea.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether buying meat in the market is the proper way to eat meat.

steps.title: Slaughter from your own animals
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your flock,' which teaches that a person should eat from his own animals, not from the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your flock.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the next פסוק, which speaks of slaughtering 'your' cattle and flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'your' shows that the ideal is to eat from animals you own. Simply buying meat whenever you feel like it is not the way the פסוק describes.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall slaughter
Cattle
Flock (sheep and goats)

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your flock."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:21. The key word is 'your': your own animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְזָבַחְתָּ מִבְּקָרְךָ וּמִצֹּאנְךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the idea raised in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One should eat meat from his own animals, not buy it in the market.

steps.title: May one slaughter all his animals to eat?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that a person might slaughter all his cattle or all his flock in order to eat meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person may slaughter all his cattle and eat, or all his flock and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another 'you might think,' setting up the next lesson from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know that a person should eat from his own animals, one might think he may use up everything he owns for meat. The ברייתא tests that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: All of his cattle
All of his flock

phrases.english: You might think he may slaughter all his cattle and eat,
[or] all his flock and eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִזְבַּח כׇּל בְּקָרוֹ וְיֹאכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 25: if one eats from his own animals, may he use up all of them?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person may slaughter everything he owns in order to eat meat.

steps.title: From your cattle, not all your cattle
steps.stepSummary: The word 'from' in 'from your cattle' and 'from your flock' teaches that one should slaughter only part, not all, of his animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'from your cattle,' and not all your cattle. It says 'from your flock,' and not all your flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by reading the small word 'from' (the letter מ) in the פסוק as meaning 'some of.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say 'your cattle' but 'from your cattle,' which means only part of them. A person should not use up his whole means of living just to eat meat.

keyTerms.meaning: From your cattle, meaning some of them
And not all

steps.whatToRemember: From the פסוקים about meat, the ברייתות learn several lessons of דרך ארץ: (1) meat should take effort, like something hunted; (2) eat it only when you truly want it; (3) eat from your own animals, not from the market; (4) never slaughter everything you own just for meat.

phrases.english: The verse says: "from your cattle," and not all your cattle,
"from your flock," and not all your flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִבְּקָרְךָ״ – וְלֹא כׇּל בְּקָרְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the idea raised in Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One should slaughter only some of his animals, never all of them, in order to eat meat.

steps.title: A spending scale for food based on wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns from the פסוק that what you eat should match what you own: vegetables, fish, meat, or a daily pot of meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: Someone who has one מנה should buy a ליטרא of vegetables for his pot. Someone with ten מנה should buy a ליטרא of fish. Someone with fifty מנה should buy a ליטרא of meat. Someone with a hundred מנה can have a pot of meat put on the fire for him every day.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the lesson that a person should not slaughter all his animals, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gives a practical scale for how much to spend on food depending on wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier דרשה taught a principle: do not use up all your resources just to eat meat. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה turns this into numbers. The richer you are, the more expensive your daily food can be, and only the very wealthy should eat meat every day.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of money equal to 100 זוז (dinars)
For his pot, meaning his daily cooked food
A unit of weight
They put a pot (of meat) on the fire for him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic Talmudic source for the idea that a person's spending on luxuries, especially meat, should match his actual means.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: From here Rabbi Elazar ben Azaria said:
One who has a maneh (one hundred dinars)
should buy a litra of vegetables for his pot;

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה מָנֶה – יִקַּח לְפָסוֹ לִיטְרָא דָּגִים,
phrases.english: ten maneh: he should buy a litra of fish for his pot;

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשִּׁים מָנֶה – יִקַּח לְפָסוֹ לִיטְרָא בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: fifty maneh: he should buy a litra of meat for his pot;

phrases.aramaic: מֵאָה מָנֶה – יִשְׁפְּתוּ לוֹ קְדֵרָה בְּכׇל יוֹם.
phrases.english: one hundred maneh: they should put a pot on the fire for him every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the lesson of step 27 (slaughter only part of your animals) as a concrete spending guide.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food spending should match wealth: daily meat only for someone with a hundred מנה.

steps.title: When do the less wealthy eat meat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the people in the lower levels of the scale get to eat meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And those others, when do they eat meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple follow-up question: if only the richest eat meat every day, when do the other people eat meat? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scale seemed to suggest that people with less money never eat meat. The גמרא wants to know if that is really true, or if there is a time when they eat it too.

keyTerms.meaning: And those others (the people lower on the scale)
When?

phrases.english: And those others, when do they eat meat?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִינָךְ אֵימַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a gap in the scale given in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How often the less wealthy people on the scale may eat meat.

steps.title: Every Friday, for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The less wealthy eat meat once a week, every ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From one ערב שבת to the next ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that everyone else eats meat once a week, for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the scale is not saying the less wealthy never eat meat. It only limits their everyday meals, while שבת still gets meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the day before שבת

phrases.english: From one Shabbat eve to the next Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They eat meat once a week, every ערב שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's scale: vegetables, fish, meat, or a daily pot of meat, depending on wealth. Everyone still has meat for שבת.

steps.title: רב: We should follow the elder's advice
steps.stepSummary: רב says we must take רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's spending advice seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: We need to be concerned about the words of the elder.
steps.whatsHappening: רב agrees with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and says people should be careful and not overspend on food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The elder" is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. רב treats his scale as real guidance for how people should live, not just a nice idea.

keyTerms.meaning: To be concerned about, to take into account
The elder, here meaning רבי אלעזר בן עזריה

phrases.english: Rav said:
We must be concerned for the words of the elder.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: צְרִיכִין אָנוּ לָחוֹשׁ לְדִבְרֵי זָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא endorses the scale from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should be careful with food spending, as רבי אלעזר בן עזריה taught.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: That works for the strong, not for us
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רב could live on a simple diet because his family was healthy, but weaker people should buy food with any money they have.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: אבא (רב) came from a family of healthy people. But people like us, if someone has even one פרוטה in his pocket, he should hurry it to the storekeeper.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits רב's advice: saving money on food only works for very healthy people. Weaker people should spend on food right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not reject the idea of being careful with money. He says it depends on the person's body. For someone who is not naturally strong, eating properly comes before saving money.

keyTerms.meaning: Healthy, strong people
The smallest coin
Storekeeper, shopkeeper
He should hurry it (rush the money over)

steps.confusionAlert: "אבא" here is not someone's father. It is רב's actual name (אבא אריכא), and רבי יוחנן is talking about him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Abba was from a family of healthy people,
phrases.notes: "Abba" is רב, the one who just spoke in the last step.

phrases.english: but people such as us,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פְּרוּטָה בְּתוֹךְ כִּיסוֹ –
phrases.english: one who has a peruta in his pocket
should hurry it to the storekeeper.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַבָּא מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת בְּרִיאִים הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's endorsement in step 31 to naturally healthy people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who are not especially strong should spend even their last coin on food.

steps.title: רב נחמן: We even borrow to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן goes further: people like him even borrow money in order to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: People like us borrow and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds an even stronger point than רבי יוחנן: weaker people should not only spend what they have on food, they even borrow to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said to spend any coin you have on food. רב נחמן goes one step further: even if you have no money, borrow for food, because staying healthy comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: We borrow
We eat

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
People such as us borrow and eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כְּגוֹן אָנוּ לוֹוִין וְאוֹכְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי יוחנן's leniency in step 32 one step further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weaker people may even borrow money to eat properly.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: be careful like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said. רבי יוחנן: that is only for the strong; others should spend their last coin on food. רב נחמן: people like us even borrow to eat.

steps.title: Lessons from the פסוק in משלי: own animals, not just land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains a פסוק in משלי: make clothing from your sheep's wool, sell a field to buy goats, and be satisfied with the milk of your own animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Lambs for your clothing": your clothing should come from the wool of your sheep. "And goats the price of a field": a person should always sell a field and buy goats, and not sell goats to buy a field. "And enough goats' milk": it is enough for a person to live off the milk of the young goats and lambs in his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new set of money lessons, explaining phrase by phrase a פסוק in משלי about running a household wisely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק becomes practical advice. Animals give wool and milk all the time, so they are a better investment than a field. A person should be satisfied with what his own animals give him, which fits the earlier theme of not overspending on food.

keyTerms.meaning: Shorn wool
Goats (he-goats)
That he supports himself, makes a living
Young goats and lambs

phrases.english: "The lambs will be for your clothing":
phrases.notes: משלי 27:26

phrases.english: your clothing should come from the shearing of lambs;
"And goats, the price of a field":

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם שָׂדֶה וְיִקַּח עַתּוּדִים,
phrases.english: a person should always sell a field and buy goats,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם עַתּוּדִים וְיִקַּח שָׂדֶה.
phrases.english: and a person should not sell goats and buy a field.
"And enough goats' milk":
phrases.notes: משלי 27:27

phrases.english: it is enough for a person that he be sustained
from the milk of young goats and lambs in his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כְּבָשִׂים לִלְבוּשֶׁךָ״ – מִגֵּז כְּבָשִׂים יְהֵא מַלְבּוּשֶׁךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new set of related lessons about household money, drawn from משלי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals are a better investment than land, and one should be satisfied with the milk of his own animals.

steps.title: Your own food comes first
steps.stepSummary: From the double wording "for your food, for the food of your household," the גמרא learns that a person's own food comes before his household's.
steps.simpleTranslation: "For your food, for the food of your household": your food comes before the food of your household.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same פסוק and learns from its order that a person must first make sure he has food for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists "your food" first and only then "the food of your household." The גמרא reads this order as a rule of priority.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes before, takes priority

phrases.english: "For your food, for the food of your household":
your food comes before the food of your household.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לְלַחְמְךָ לְלֶחֶם בֵּיתֶךָ״ – לַחְמְךָ קוֹדֶם לְלֶחֶם בֵּיתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's own food takes priority over the food of his household.

steps.title: Don't get your children used to meat and wine
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא learns from "and sustenance for your maidens" that a person should give his children basic food and not get them used to meat and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And life for your maidens": מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said: Give life to your young ones. From here the תורה taught proper behavior: a person should not get his son used to meat and wine.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא explains the last phrase of the פסוק as advice about raising children: feed them simply, not with expensive foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads "נערותיך" as "your young ones," meaning your children. Giving them "life" means plain, healthy food, so they don't grow used to costly meat and wine. This ties back to the whole סוגיא's theme of not overspending on luxuries.

keyTerms.meaning: Your maidens; here read as your young ones, your children
Proper conduct, wise everyday behavior
Accustom, train (here: get someone used to something)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוקים in משלי teach: own animals rather than just land, be satisfied with what your animals give, your food comes first, and don't get your children used to meat and wine.

phrases.english: "And sustenance for your maidens":

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman said:
Give sustenance to your young ones,
from here the Torah taught proper behavior

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ בָּשָׂר וְיַיִן.
phrases.english: that a person should not accustom his son to meat and wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְחַיִּים לְנַעֲרוֹתֶיךָ״ – אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the final phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should not accustom his children to meat and wine.

steps.title: Opening a new statement from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new statement by רבי יוחנן, continuing the practical advice about money and daily living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup: the גמרא is telling us that רבי יוחנן is about to speak. His actual words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been taught yet; this line only names the speaker. Because it follows a series of teachings about spending wisely on food and household needs, expect רבי יוחנן's words to add more practical advice of the same kind.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement or teaching said by a sage; this line opens one
A sage of the גמרא period, like רבי יוחנן, whose statements the גמרא records
Practical, sensible conduct in everyday life, the theme of this section

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a teaching in this line. It only tells you who is speaking; the content comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מר זוטרא's advice about feeding children simply, the גמרא moves on to another sage's practical advice by naming רבי יוחנן as the next speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces רבי יוחנן's coming statement.
